content:
I upgraded to the Apple Watch Series 12 last week, and after testing it for a few days, three features left a deep impression on me.

#1: The S11 Chip Makes Everything Faster

It was high time Apple updated the chip on the Apple Watch, because Apple made no changes at all last year, and there hasn't been any real performance upgrade since the S9.

I'm glad to say the new S11 chip is noticeably faster and more powerful than the previous-generation S10.

Everyday operations on the Apple Watch Series 12 just feel fast. And the headline watchOS 27 feature, Siri AI, is a particularly good fit on this latest hardware. I've tested it, and Siri runs really slowly on older hardware, but the performance on the Series 12 is much closer to what I'd expect.

#2: Brand-New Health Features and Watch Face Complications

The new health sensor system should allow the Apple Watch Series 12 to more accurately track important metrics like heart rate and steps. But this time, the improvements go well beyond just better accuracy.

Thanks to the new health sensors, the Series 12 offers three watch face complications that weren't available before:

  • Heart Rate
  • Daily Steps
  • Readiness

You can view your latest heart rate, steps, and readiness score right on the watch face.

I've been testing the heart rate syncing data complication, but readiness will need a bit more data before I can use it. Overall, these are very practical new features that meaningfully enhance the Apple Watch's health and wellness capabilities.

#3: Faster Charging

The overall battery life of the Apple Watch Series 12 is similar to the Series 11, but you can get up to 25% more time during outdoor workouts.

Longer battery life is always a good thing, but I'm even more impressed by the Series 12's fast charging. Here's how it compares to the Series 11:

  • Apple Watch Series 12: 15 minutes of charging delivers up to 12 hours of use
  • Apple Watch Series 11: 15 minutes of charging delivers up to 8 hours of use

I usually wear my Apple Watch to sleep and try to give it a quick top-up at night, but I often forget to leave it on the charger long enough. With the Series 12's fast charging, those bad habits of mine are no longer a problem.

If you want to see more reviews of the Series 12, you can check out my colleague Chance's full review here.

The Apple Watch Series 12 is now on sale, starting at $399.

Have you upgraded to the Apple Watch Series 12? Why or why not? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
